queries.file: Return indexed metadata, semantic evidence, ownership, history/hotspot metadata, ranked structural tests, and incoming/outgoing graph relationships for an exact repository path.
queries.symbol: Find symbols by exact or substring name and return definitions plus owning files.
queries.deps: Return forward code/build/workflow/dependency/artifact relationships from a file with optional transitive traversal.
queries.rdeps: Return reverse dependencies / affected consumers from a file with optional transitive traversal.
queries.impact: Given changed paths or a Git base, return impacted files, subsystems, ranked tests, workflows, security zones, dependencies, architecture findings, capabilities and explicitly affected artifacts.
queries.diff: Combine Git path change status with current-head graph and reverse-impact evidence for review automation.
queries.dependency: Query canonical external dependency components and their structured manifest declarations.
queries.route: Query discoverable backend HTTP and Expo file-route surfaces with source paths.
queries.env: Query environment-variable names and reference paths; values are never indexed.
queries.hotspot: Return relative engineering-attention hotspots derived from bounded history, dependency degree, size and risk metadata.
queries.batch: Return 100-batch plan entries with handoff-evidence presence and dependency-note state without inferring completion.
queries.tests: Return ranked structurally relevant test files for an exact or matching source path, with confidence, precision, depth and reason evidence.
queries.artifact: Query explicit container-stage and Compose-service artifacts plus unresolved Docker build selectors; arbitrary shell outputs are not inferred.
queries.search: Deterministic lexical retrieval over paths, symbols, imports, routes, environment names, package declarations and subsystems.
queries.owner: Return files associated with architectural ownership zones or approximate local CODEOWNERS evidence.
queries.capability: Return structural evidence, batch ownership and missing evidence for a game-creation capability.
queries.security: Return security controls, sensitive surfaces and findings connected to paths or subsystems.
queries.build: Return entry points, manifests, package scripts, Make targets, workflows, referenced repository files, explicit artifacts and build-affecting relationships.

precision.javascript_typescript: conservative lexical imports/exports until SCIP/compiler ingestion is enabled
precision.manifests: structured parser evidence for supported Python/npm manifests; Docker/Actions use constrained declarations
precision.workflow_build_links: lexical references to tracked repository paths, Python modules and Make targets
precision.test_evidence: Direct AST imports are strongest; lexical, explicit structural links and bounded transitive imports are separately labeled and ranked without claiming coverage.
precision.artifact_lineage: Dockerfile COPY/ADD/stage relationships plus explicit Compose build contexts/targets; directory selectors are bounded nodes and dynamic/glob/missing inputs remain unresolved.
precision.routes: FastAPI-style decorators and Expo file routing are discoverability evidence, not reachability proof
precision.history: bounded Git history relative to HEAD commit time for deterministic churn/freshness signals
precision.other: metadata-only unless a specialized indexer is registered

non_claims: Structural evidence is not correctness or release-readiness proof.
Ranked test confidence is structural relevance, not coverage, pass probability or proof of sufficiency.
Focused test ranking never authorizes skipping required integration or release gates.
Artifact lineage from declarations does not prove a built artifact is reproducible or attested.
Arbitrary shell outputs are never inferred as artifact lineage.
Hotspot scores are triage signals, not quality or security grades.
Batch note presence does not mean completion.
Offline dependency declarations do not replace GitHub Dependency Graph or Dependabot resolved vulnerability evidence.
Environment variable values are never part of the index.
